careers.parliamentaryService: Elected to the Senate for Queensland at the 2013 election and re-elected in 2016 and 2022. The Parliament of Australia records no state parliamentary service and no casual-vacancy appointment. He was a cabinet minister in the Turnbull and Morrison governments from February 2016, standing aside from the ministry on 25 July 2017 during the section 44 citizenship reference and returning on 27 October 2017, the day the High Court ruled he was validly elected; he left the ministry on 3 February 2020. He served as Nationals Whip in the Senate in 2015-16 and 2025-26 and as Deputy Leader of The Nationals in the Senate from 2019 to 2022, and is recorded as Leader of the Federal Parliamentary Nationals from 11 March 2026, with a shadow cabinet portfolio from 16 March 2026.

integrityMatters.title: High Court ruling that Senator Canavan was not disqualified under section 44(i) of the Constitution (Re Canavan)
integrityMatters.organisation: High Court of Australia sitting as the Court of Disputed Returns, on a reference from the Senate
integrityMatters.description: In July 2017 Senator Canavan disclosed that he might hold Italian citizenship by descent, registered by his mother in 2006 without his knowledge, and stood aside from the ministry while the question was tested. The Senate referred the question of whether he was incapable of being chosen under section 44(i) to the High Court sitting as the Court of Disputed Returns, alongside references concerning six other parliamentarians. On 27 October 2017 the court held that, on the evidence of Italian law before it, one could not be satisfied that he had ever been an Italian citizen, and answered that there was no vacancy in his Senate place. He returned to the ministry the same day.

statusHistory.note: Senator Canavan announced that his mother had registered him as an Italian citizen in 2006 without his knowledge and stood aside from the ministry; the Attorney-General said the matter would be referred to the High Court.

The Senate referred questions concerning his qualification to the Court of Disputed Returns (the judgment records the President of the Senate's letter of 9 August 2017). His renunciation of any Italian citizenship took effect on 8 August 2017.
The Full Court unanimously answered that there was no vacancy by reason of section 44(i) in the Queensland Senate place for which he was returned. He resumed his cabinet post the same day.

integrityMatters.outcome: Order of the Court of Disputed Returns: 'There is no vacancy by reason of s 44(i) of the Constitution in the representation of Queensland in the Senate for the place for which Senator the Hon Matthew Canavan was returned.' Reasons at [86]: 'On the evidence before the Court, one cannot be satisfied that Senator Canavan was a citizen of Italy.'

integrityMatters.title: Auditor-General's audit of the Community Sport Infrastructure Program and the finding by the Secretary of the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet that Senator McKenzie breached the Statement of Ministerial Standards
integrityMatters.organisation: Australian National Audit Office (Auditor-General Report No. 23 of 2019-20); Secretary of the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet, advising the Prime Minister under the Statement of Ministerial Standards
integrityMatters.description: On 15 January 2020 the Auditor-General reported on the $100 million Community Sport Infrastructure Program, administered by Sport Australia with Senator McKenzie, as Minister for Sport, approving the grants. The report found that funding decisions departed from Sport Australia's merit assessments, that the approach documented in the minister's office focused on marginal and targeted electorates, and that there was no evident legal authority for the minister's approval role. The Prime Minister asked the Secretary of the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet to advise whether the Statement of Ministerial Standards had been breached. The Secretary advised that she had acted within the program guidelines and had not breached the Standards with respect to fairness, but that she had breached them by failing to declare her membership of two organisations and had an actual, undeclared and unmanaged conflict of interest in awarding $35,980 to the Wangaratta Clay Target Club, of which she was a member. She resigned from the ministry and as Deputy Leader of the Nationals on 2 February 2020 and remained in the Senate.

statusHistory.note: Auditor-General's report presented to Parliament: the award of grant funding was not informed by an appropriate assessment process and sound advice, successful applications were not those assessed as most meritorious, there was evidence of distribution bias toward marginal and targeted electorates, and no evident legal authority for the minister to approve the grants.

The Prime Minister sought advice from the Secretary of the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet under paragraph 7.4 of the Statement of Ministerial Standards on any apparent breaches in relation to the minister's administration of the program.

The Prime Minister announced the Secretary's conclusion that Senator McKenzie had breached the Standards by failing to declare memberships of two organisations and had an actual, undeclared and unmanaged conflict of interest in awarding a grant to the Wangaratta Clay Target Club, while finding no breach with respect to fairness. She resigned from the ministry and as Deputy Leader of the Nationals the same day.

integrityMatters.outcome: Secretary of the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet, as stated in his submission to the Senate Select Committee: 'I concluded Senator McKenzie did not act in breach of the Standards with respect to fairness. I did find that Senator McKenzie breached the Standards by failing to declare her memberships of two organisations and that she had an actual conflict of interest when awarding funding to one of those organisations, the Wangaratta Clay Target Club, which was neither declared to the Prime Minister nor managed.' Senator McKenzie resigned from the ministry on 2 February 2020. The Secretary's full report has not been published.

integrityMatters.title: Senate Select Committee on Administration of Sports Grants: inquiry, evidence by order of the Senate, and final report
integrityMatters.organisation: Senate of Australia; Senate Select Committee on Administration of Sports Grants
integrityMatters.description: On 5 February 2020 the Senate established a select committee to inquire into the administration and award of funding under the Community Sport Infrastructure Grant program, and separately ordered the production of the Secretary's report on Senator McKenzie, which the government declined to table on Cabinet-confidentiality grounds. The committee tabled an interim report on 1 December 2020 concerning public interest immunity claims and, by order of the Senate, took evidence from Senator McKenzie on 12 February 2021, when she told the committee she was solely responsible for the decisions. Its final report of 18 March 2021, supported by the Labor, Greens and crossbench majority, concluded that she applied politically motivated considerations inconsistent with the published guidelines and that her legal authority to make the decisions remained in doubt. Coalition senators dissented, describing the program as a success and relying on the Secretary's finding of no breach with respect to fairness. The Senate imposed no sanction, and no privileges or senators' interests committee matter was located.

statusHistory.note: The Senate established the select committee and ordered production of the Secretary's report; the government claimed public interest immunity and the order was recorded as not complied with. A further order on 25 February 2020 met the same claim.
After the interim report of 1 December 2020, the Senate ordered Senator McKenzie to appear before the committee; she gave evidence on 12 February 2021.

Final report tabled with nine recommendations. The majority concluded the minister applied politically motivated considerations inconsistent with the guidelines; Coalition senators' minority report rejected this. The government's response was received on 21 May 2026.

integrityMatters.outcome: Majority report, paragraph 4.77: 'Given the minister has not been able to provide any credible or documented rationale for her decision making the committee can only conclude that she applied considerations that were politically motivated and inconsistent with the published guidelines.' Chapter 3: 'the question of the minister's legal authority to have made decisions on grants under the CSIG program remains under considerable doubt.' Coalition senators' minority report: the program 'was an outstanding success' and the senator's evidence 'was clear, confident and compelling'. No sanction was imposed by the Senate.
